name: Projected Distinguishing Range of Singletons
proof: On the full domain, omitting two coordinates $i,j$ makes the singleton concepts $\{i\}$ and $\{j\}$ have the same empty trace, so every distinguishing coordinate set has size at least $n-1$. Retaining all but one coordinate gives distinct traces for all n singleton concepts, so this bound is attained. A projection to k<n coordinates consists of its k singleton traces together with the empty trace, and every retained coordinate is needed to distinguish its singleton from the empty trace; its distinguishing range is therefore k\leq n-1. The full projection has the already calculated value n-1.
